about: The muscles of the shoulder and the upper arm, drawn against the clavicle, the shoulder blade and the humerus of the shoulder and arm bone atlas: the deltoid over the shoulder, the four muscles of the rotator cuff, the teres major, the coracobrachialis, the biceps and brachialis in front of the arm and the triceps behind it, each from its origin to its insertion as Gray's gives them. The radius and ulna are not in this skeleton, so the biceps, brachialis and triceps end in a short tendon at the elbow. Inside the biceps are magnified schematics of muscle tissue and of the neuromuscular junction, drawn far larger than life. The drives are the whole-body ones the engine has: muscle tone (raised in rigidity, lost in paralysis, which is how a neuromuscular blocker acts), exertion, shivering and a seizure. Arm movement, the forearm and force are not simulated.

parts.label: Deltoid
parts.summary: The rounded muscle that caps the shoulder
parts.function: The deltoid covers the shoulder joint and runs from the clavicle, the acromion and the spine of the scapula to the deltoid tuberosity of the humerus. It lifts the arm away from the side, and its front and back parts also swing it forward and back.

drives.note: Exertion is the fraction of aerobic capacity in use; the textbook says working skeletal muscle takes most of the extra blood flow and oxygen of exercise, so a muscle used in effort rises with it. The weight is a display scale and not a muscle force.
Shivering is rhythmic contraction of skeletal muscle that makes heat; the textbook describes it as a whole-body muscle response, so this muscle rises with it. The weight is a display scale.
Raised skeletal muscle tone (rigidity) is a rise in the tone of the muscles of the body, so a muscle of this group tightens with it. The weight is a display scale.

Lost skeletal muscle tone (paralysis) lowers the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle goes slack. A drug that blocks the neuromuscular junction reaches this muscle through that same fall in tone. The weight is a display scale.
A generalised seizure drives the skeletal muscles into strong, repeated contraction, so a muscle of this group contracts with it. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Anterior (Clavicular) Part
parts.summary: The front part of the deltoid, from the clavicle
parts.function: The anterior part arises from the lateral part of the clavicle and helps to flex and turn the arm inward.

parts.label: Middle (Acromial) Part
parts.summary: The middle part of the deltoid, from the acromion
parts.function: The middle part arises from the acromion and is the main part that lifts the arm out to the side.

parts.label: Posterior (Spinal) Part
parts.summary: The back part of the deltoid, from the spine of the scapula
parts.function: The posterior part arises from the spine of the scapula and helps to extend and turn the arm outward.

parts.label: Rotator Cuff
parts.summary: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis, with their tendons round the humeral head
parts.function: These four muscles run from the shoulder blade to the head of the humerus, and their tendons blend with the capsule of the shoulder joint. Together they hold the head of the humerus in its shallow socket while the arm moves. The thin cap drawn here is the place where the four tendons blend into the capsule.

parts.function: The supraspinatus arises from the supraspinous fossa and runs under the acromion to the superior facet of the greater tubercle. It starts the arm lifting away from the side and holds the humeral head in the socket.

parts.summary: The muscle in the fossa below the spine of the scapula
parts.function: The infraspinatus arises from the infraspinous fossa and runs to the middle facet of the greater tubercle. It turns the arm outward and holds the humeral head in the socket.

parts.summary: The small round muscle on the lateral border of the scapula
parts.function: The teres minor arises from the dorsal surface of the lateral border of the scapula and runs to the inferior facet of the greater tubercle. It turns the arm outward and holds the humeral head in the socket.

parts.summary: The broad muscle on the front of the shoulder blade
parts.function: The subscapularis fills the subscapular fossa on the front of the scapula and runs in front of the shoulder joint to the lesser tubercle. It turns the arm inward and holds the humeral head in the socket.

parts.label: Teres Major
parts.summary: The thick round muscle from the lower shoulder blade to the humerus
parts.function: The teres major arises from the dorsal surface of the inferior angle of the scapula and passes behind and then in front of the humerus to the medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus. It draws the raised arm down and turns it inward.

parts.function: The coracobrachialis arises from the tip of the coracoid process, together with the short head of the biceps, and runs to the middle of the medial surface of the humeral shaft. It draws the arm forward and toward the body.

parts.label: Biceps Brachii
parts.summary: The two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm
parts.function: The biceps arises by two heads from the scapula and runs down the front of the arm in front of the brachialis. At the elbow its tendon goes on to the radius, which this skeleton does not draw, so the muscle is shown ending in a short tendon. It bends the elbow and turns the forearm so that the palm faces up.

parts.label: Long Head
parts.summary: The head that arises inside the shoulder joint
parts.function: The long head arises from the supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula, and its tendon passes over the humeral head and down the intertubercular sulcus before it joins the belly of the muscle.

parts.label: Tendon in the Intertubercular Sulcus
parts.summary: The tendon of the long head, held in the groove between the tubercles
parts.function: The tendon runs from the supraglenoid tubercle over the humeral head and lies in the intertubercular sulcus between the greater and lesser tubercles. The groove holds it in place as the arm moves.

parts.label: Short Head
parts.summary: The head that arises from the coracoid process
parts.function: The short head arises from the tip of the coracoid process, with the coracobrachialis, and joins the long head in the belly of the biceps.

parts.label: Tendon from the Coracoid Process
parts.summary: The tendon of the short head, shared at its start with the coracobrachialis
parts.function: This tendon runs from the tip of the coracoid process down in front of the shoulder to the belly of the short head.

parts.label: Brachialis
parts.summary: The muscle under the biceps on the front of the humerus
parts.function: The brachialis arises from the front of the lower half of the humerus and lies directly on the bone beneath the biceps. It goes on to the ulna, which this skeleton does not draw, so it is shown ending in a short tendon at the elbow. It bends the elbow.

parts.label: Triceps Brachii
parts.summary: The three-headed muscle on the back of the upper arm
parts.function: The triceps arises by three heads from the scapula and the back of the humerus and runs down the back of the arm. Its tendon goes on to the olecranon of the ulna, which this skeleton does not draw, so the muscle is shown ending in a short tendon behind the elbow. It straightens the elbow.

parts.label: Long Head
parts.summary: The head that arises from the scapula below the shoulder socket
parts.function: The long head arises from the infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula and runs down the back of the arm. It is the only head that crosses the shoulder joint.

parts.label: Lateral Head
parts.summary: The head that arises from the back of the humerus above the radial groove
parts.function: The lateral head arises from the back of the humerus above the groove for the radial nerve and lies outside the long head.

parts.label: Medial Head
parts.summary: The deepest head, on the back of the humerus below the radial groove
parts.function: The medial head arises from the back of the humerus below the radial groove and lies directly on the bone, under the other two heads.

parts.label: Common Tendon
parts.summary: The tendon the three heads share
parts.function: The three heads join one broad tendon that runs to the olecranon of the ulna, so they act together to straighten the elbow.

parts.label: Fascicle (enlarged)
parts.summary: A bundle of muscle fibres with the connective tissue sleeves round it
parts.function: A skeletal muscle is made of fascicles, each a bundle of fibres. Connective tissue sleeves hold the fibres together and carry the vessels and nerves. This is a magnified schematic, drawn far larger than life and placed inside the biceps so that it can be seen; it is not true size or place.

parts.label: Epimysium
parts.summary: The connective tissue sleeve round the whole muscle
parts.function: The epimysium wraps the whole muscle and is continuous with its tendons. It lets the muscle slide against its neighbours.

parts.label: Perimysium
parts.summary: The connective tissue sleeve round each fascicle
parts.function: The perimysium divides the muscle into fascicles and carries the larger vessels and nerves between them.

parts.label: Endomysium
parts.summary: The thin connective tissue sleeve round each muscle fibre
parts.function: The endomysium lies between neighbouring fibres and carries the fine vessels that feed them.

parts.label: Skeletal Muscle Fibre (enlarged)
parts.summary: One long, many-nucleated muscle cell
parts.function: A skeletal muscle fibre is a single long cell that is packed with myofibrils, the contractile units, and is run by one motor nerve ending. A signal that spreads over its membrane and into the cell makes the myofibrils shorten. This is a magnified schematic, drawn far larger than life and placed inside the biceps so that it can be seen; it is not true size or place.

parts.label: Sarcolemma
parts.summary: The cell membrane of the muscle fibre
parts.function: The sarcolemma carries the electrical signal along the fibre and down into it through the transverse tubules.

parts.label: Transverse (T) Tubules
parts.summary: Tubes that carry the surface signal into the fibre
parts.function: The transverse tubules are inward folds of the sarcolemma that pass between the myofibrils. They carry the signal deep into the fibre so that every myofibril is reached together.

parts.label: Sarcoplasmic Reticulum
parts.summary: The store of calcium that wraps each myofibril
parts.function: The sarcoplasmic reticulum is a membrane network round the myofibrils that stores calcium and releases it when the signal arrives, then takes it back so the fibre relaxes.

parts.label: Terminal Cisternae
parts.summary: The swollen ends of the sarcoplasmic reticulum beside the T tubules
parts.function: The terminal cisternae lie on each side of a transverse tubule and release the stored calcium when the signal reaches them.

parts.label: Peripheral Nuclei
parts.summary: The many nuclei lying just under the sarcolemma
parts.function: A muscle fibre has many nuclei, and they lie at its edge under the membrane, out of the way of the myofibrils.

parts.label: Mitochondria
parts.summary: The cell's power plants, packed between the myofibrils
parts.function: Mitochondria between the myofibrils make most of the energy that the contracting fibre uses.

parts.label: Myofibrils
parts.summary: The long contractile threads that fill the fibre
parts.function: Each myofibril is a chain of sarcomeres end to end. The shortening of all the sarcomeres in a chain is what shortens the fibre.

parts.label: Satellite Cell
parts.summary: A small stem cell lying against the fibre under its basement membrane
parts.function: A satellite cell is a resting cell beside a fibre that can divide and add to the fibre when the muscle is damaged or grows.

parts.label: Sarcomere (enlarged)
parts.summary: The repeating unit of contraction between two Z discs
parts.function: A sarcomere is the stretch of a myofibril between two Z discs. Thin filaments run in from each Z disc and thick filaments lie between them. When the filaments slide past each other the sarcomere shortens. This is a magnified schematic, drawn far larger than life and placed inside the biceps so that it can be seen; it is not true size or place.

parts.label: Z Discs
parts.summary: The plates that mark the ends of the sarcomere
parts.function: The Z discs anchor the thin filaments and mark the two ends of the sarcomere. They are drawn closer together as the sarcomere shortens.

parts.label: I Band
parts.summary: The light band that holds thin filaments only
parts.function: The I band is the part of the sarcomere where there are only thin filaments. It is a half band on each side of a Z disc and narrows as the sarcomere shortens.

parts.label: A Band
parts.summary: The dark band as long as the thick filaments
parts.function: The A band is the whole length of the thick filaments, including where the thin filaments overlap them. Its length does not change as the sarcomere shortens.

parts.label: H Zone
parts.summary: The middle of the A band where thick filaments lie alone
parts.function: The H zone is the centre of the A band that the thin filaments do not reach at rest. It closes up as they slide in.

parts.label: M Line
parts.summary: The line across the middle that holds the thick filaments in register
parts.function: The M line lies at the centre of the H zone and links the thick filaments side to side.

parts.label: Thin Filaments (actin)
parts.summary: The actin filaments that run in from each Z disc
parts.function: The thin filaments are made mainly of actin and are fixed to the Z disc. They slide in between the thick filaments when the fibre contracts.

parts.label: Troponin
parts.summary: The calcium-binding complex on the thin filament
parts.function: Troponin sits on the thin filament at regular intervals. When it binds calcium it changes shape and so lets the myosin heads reach the actin.

parts.label: Tropomyosin
parts.summary: The strand that lies along the thin filament
parts.function: Tropomyosin lies along the groove of the thin filament and covers the sites where myosin heads would bind, until calcium binds troponin.

parts.label: Thick Filaments (myosin)
parts.summary: The myosin filaments in the centre of the sarcomere
parts.function: The thick filaments are bundles of myosin. They lie in the A band and hold the heads that reach out to the thin filaments.

parts.label: Myosin Heads
parts.summary: The heads that reach from the thick filament to the actin
parts.function: The myosin heads bind to actin, bend, and release again, over and over, which pulls the thin filaments toward the centre. They draw on the cell's energy store to do it.

parts.label: Titin
parts.summary: The elastic protein that links each Z disc to the thick filament
parts.function: Titin is a long elastic protein that holds the thick filaments centred between the Z discs and returns the sarcomere to its length after it is stretched.

parts.label: Neuromuscular Junction (enlarged)
parts.summary: Where a motor nerve ending meets a muscle fibre
parts.function: The motor nerve ending releases acetylcholine into a narrow cleft, and the acetylcholine opens channels in the muscle fibre's end plate, which starts the contraction. Each fibre is run by one such junction. At this junction a competitive nicotinic blocker holds the receptor without opening it, so the end plate is not depolarised; a depolarising blocker acts like acetylcholine but is not removed as quickly, so the end plate stays depolarised and cannot answer the next signal; and an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor lets acetylcholine linger in the cleft. This describes how they act and is not advice. This is a magnified schematic, drawn far larger than life and placed inside the biceps so that it can be seen; it is not true size or place.

parts.label: Motor Axon Terminal
parts.summary: The swollen end of the motor nerve fibre
parts.function: The terminal holds the vesicles of acetylcholine and releases them into the cleft when the nerve signal arrives.

parts.label: Synaptic Vesicles (acetylcholine)
parts.summary: Small packets of acetylcholine in the terminal
parts.function: Each vesicle holds acetylcholine. When the signal arrives vesicles empty into the cleft, and they are drawn moving to the cleft face in step with the activity of the muscle.

parts.label: Synaptic Cleft
parts.summary: The narrow gap between the nerve ending and the muscle fibre
parts.function: Acetylcholine crosses the synaptic cleft in a very short time and is then broken down.

parts.label: Acetylcholinesterase
parts.summary: The enzyme in the cleft that breaks acetylcholine down
parts.function: Acetylcholinesterase lies in the cleft and splits acetylcholine, so that each signal is brief and the end plate can answer the next one.

parts.label: Motor End Plate
parts.summary: The part of the muscle fibre membrane under the nerve ending
parts.function: The motor end plate is the specialised patch of the sarcolemma under the nerve terminal. It is folded and is the part that responds to acetylcholine.

parts.label: Junctional Folds
parts.summary: The deep folds of the end plate under the terminal
parts.function: The junctional folds greatly increase the area of membrane that faces the cleft and carry the receptors on their crests.

parts.label: Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors
parts.summary: The acetylcholine-gated channels of the end plate
parts.function: When two acetylcholine molecules bind a receptor its channel opens and positive ions flow into the fibre, which depolarises the end plate. Blocking or occupying these receptors is how neuromuscular blocking drugs act.

parts.label: Terminal Schwann Cell
parts.summary: The cell that caps the nerve terminal
parts.function: A terminal Schwann cell covers the nerve ending on the side away from the muscle and helps keep the junction in place.

parts.label: Muscle Spindle (enlarged)
parts.summary: A stretch sensor lying among the muscle fibres
parts.function: A muscle spindle is a small capsule of thin, specialised muscle fibres with sensory nerve endings wound round them. It reports how long the muscle is and how fast the length is changing. This is a magnified schematic, drawn far larger than life and placed inside the biceps so that it can be seen; it is not true size or place.

drives.note: Exertion is the fraction of aerobic capacity in use; the textbook says working skeletal muscle takes most of the extra blood flow and oxygen of exercise, so a muscle used in effort rises with it. The weight is a display scale and not a muscle force.
Shivering is rhythmic contraction of skeletal muscle that makes heat; the textbook describes it as a whole-body muscle response, so this muscle rises with it. The weight is a display scale.

Lost skeletal muscle tone (paralysis) lowers the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle goes slack. A drug that blocks the neuromuscular junction reaches this muscle through that same fall in tone. The weight is a display scale.
A generalised seizure drives the skeletal muscles into strong, repeated contraction, so a muscle of this group contracts with it. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Golgi Tendon Organ (enlarged)
parts.summary: A tension sensor at the junction of muscle and tendon
parts.function: A Golgi tendon organ is a sensory nerve ending woven among the tendon strands where muscle joins tendon. It reports the tension the muscle is pulling with. This is a magnified schematic, drawn far larger than life and placed inside the biceps so that it can be seen; it is not true size or place.

drives.note: Exertion is the fraction of aerobic capacity in use; the textbook says working skeletal muscle takes most of the extra blood flow and oxygen of exercise, so a muscle used in effort rises with it. The weight is a display scale and not a muscle force.
Shivering is rhythmic contraction of skeletal muscle that makes heat; the textbook describes it as a whole-body muscle response, so this muscle rises with it. The weight is a display scale.
Raised skeletal muscle tone (rigidity) is a rise in the tone of the muscles of the body, so a muscle of this group tightens with it. The weight is a display scale.
A generalised seizure drives the skeletal muscles into strong, repeated contraction, so a muscle of this group contracts with it. The weight is a display scale.
